source.quote: we have decided to push back the deprecation date to November 12, 2025.

tasks.reasoning:
This one task covers all 2 slack changes that affect this repo. Handle every one of them in this single change set, prove each with your test, and say in finish which you changed and which needed no change.

1. files.upload API method sunset (deadline pushed to Nov 12, 2025); migrate to files.getUploadURLExternal / files.completeUploadExternal (files_upload_v2 in Python SDK) (endpoint-removed, effective 2025-11-12)
   Source: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog
   Quote: we have decided to push back the deprecation date to November 12, 2025.
   Affects: operations: files.upload, files_upload
   Call sites: Tableau2Slack.py:99 (Calls files_upload (files.upload), which Slack sunsets on 2025-11-12. The call will fail once the method is removed. It passes channels/file/title/filetype and reads file.url_private from the response.)
   Why it applies: The repo's only file upload goes through the removed files.upload method. Moving to slack_sdk does not fix this, because the call must be rewritten to files_upload_v2 (or files.getUploadURLExternal and files.completeUploadExternal) in a separate edit. slackclient 2.5.0 has no files_upload_v2, so the migration agent should either do this on top of the slack_sdk upgrade or call the new methods through api_call. Things to check: v2 takes `channel` or `channels` and `file`, `title` and `filename` (filetype is not used the same way); the response shape differs (a `file` or `files` entry), so the code that reads file.url_private must be re-verified; and the bot token needs files:write. The deadline has probably already passed, so uploads may already be failing.

2. PyPI slackclient (2.x) is in maintenance mode; successor slack_sdk v3 renames the package, deprecates `slack.*` imports, drops required aiohttp and changes WebClient (no run_async) (sdk-major, effective 2020-11)
   Source: https://docs.slack.dev/tools/python-slack-sdk/v3-migration/
   Quote: The PyPI project has been renamed from slackclient to slack_sdk.
   Affects: operations: WebClient, LegacyWebClient, AsyncWebClient, run_async; versions: <3.0.0, 3.0.0; sdk: slackclient
   Call sites: Tableau2Slack.py:96 (WebClient is built from the slackclient package (`slack.WebClient`). It must change to `from slack_sdk import WebClient` after the rename.); Tableau2Slack.py:99 (A WebClient method call on the slackclient 2.5.0 pin. It keeps working after the move, but the files_upload rewrite is a separate task.); Tableau2Slack.py:141 (chat_postMessage on the slackclient WebClient. It is the same call in slack_sdk, but it needs a check after the import change.)
   Why it applies: The repo pins slackclient == 2.5.0, which is in maintenance mode. The successor package, slack_sdk, replaces the `slack.*` imports. The upgrade is to replace slackclient with slack_sdk in the requirements and change the imports. The code does not use run_async, so there is no sync/async change to make. This is not breaking today, so it is low urgency, but the old package gets no new features such as files_upload_v2.

chat_postMessage on the slackclient WebClient. It is the same call in slack_sdk, but it needs a check after the import change.

record.prBody:
## 2 changes: files.upload API method sunset (deadline pushed to Nov 12, 2025); migrate to files.getUploadURLExternal / files.completeUploadExternal (files_upload_v2 in Python SDK) and more [Verified]

### Change

Replaced slackclient==2.5.0 with slack_sdk>=3.19.0,<4; imports moved to slack_sdk. files_upload became files_upload_v2(channel=<ID from new env var slackUploadChannelId>, file, title), with filetype dropped. The response is now read as img.get("file") or img["files"][0]. chat_postMessage is unchanged. Added slackUploadChannelId to example.env and added tests/test_slack_sdk.py.

Files touched:
- `Tableau2Slack.py`
- `example.env`
- `requirements.txt`
- `tests/test_slack_sdk.py`

### Why

files.upload is sunset on 2025-11-12, and slackclient 2.5.0 has no files_upload_v2, so the SDK had to move to slack_sdk in the same change.

> we have decided to push back the deprecation date to November 12, 2025.

Source: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| slack-sdk-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- slack-sdk-test, added by the agent: `python tests/test_slack_sdk.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `slack-sdk-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The v2 response shape (file vs files[0]) and whether url_private works right away in the following chat_postMessage were not checked live.
- README and documentation were not checked for mentions of the old #tableau-test channel.
- The slackclient to slack_sdk swap and the nest_asyncio leftover were not run against the real Tableau and Slack flow. nest_asyncio was left in place.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- New required env var slackUploadChannelId: a channel ID like C0123456789, replacing the hardcoded '#tableau-test'. The bot must be a member of that channel.
- Bot scopes needed: files:write and chat:write. chat:write.customize is needed to keep the username and icon_url overrides.
- filetype='png' is no longer passed; Slack infers the type.

review.summary: The diff swaps files_upload for files_upload_v2 and moves imports to slack_sdk, which is the right direction. The 'verified' grade rests on a test that only parses the source and checks that attributes exist; it never makes a call. Several behaviour changes follow from the migration and are not covered. files_upload_v2's `file`, `title` and `channel` parameters are not confirmed here, so check them against the SDK types. Pre-existing and not part of this change: the blanket `except:` hides failures, and the old pins (requests 2.22.0, nest-asyncio 1.3.3) may not work with slack_sdk.

concerns.issue: The upload channel is now read from the new env var slackUploadChannelId with no default or validation. If it is unset, channel=None and the upload may succeed without sharing to a channel. url_private may then not be usable, or the call may fail. Existing deployments with a .env that lacks the variable will break or change behaviour silently. The old hardcoded '#tableau-test' is gone.

files_upload_v2 is asynchronous in effect (getUploadURLExternal, then a POST, then completeUploadExternal). The returned file object may not yet have url_private populated, or the image may not be fully processed when chat_postMessage runs immediately afterwards. The fallback `img.get('file') or img['files'][0]` is untested against a real response shape.

The test is purely static (AST checks plus hasattr). It does not exercise the upload, the response parsing, or chat_postMessage. The 'verified' grade overstates what it proves. The test file also runs top-level asserts rather than using a test framework, and it opens the source file without closing it.

The `filetype='png'` argument was dropped. The SDK may infer the type from the filename, but this is unconfirmed. Also, files_upload_v2 needs the files:write scope and the bot must be a member of the channel, so the bot token's permissions may need updating.

Replacing slackclient 2.5.0 with slack_sdk >=3.19.0 changes a pinned dependency to a range, so installs are not reproducible. slack_sdk 3.x also needs a newer Python and aiohttp, and may conflict with nest-asyncio 1.3.3 and the other old pins. This has not been checked with a full install.

The chat_postMessage call (line 141) is unchanged. It keeps working under slack_sdk, and the diff makes no change for the named call site. Passing blocks and attachments as json.dumps strings is accepted but was not tested.
